intro: Each merge to main bumps the patch version. A minor version marks a milestone.

notes: The next milestone is every iced example, and every example in `examples/`, running under `rawr run` through importer-generated bindings only.

entries.text: rawr-import's driver builds again on nightly-2026-11-10 and every other nightly in its window. CI now builds it on the window's newest nightly too.

A save of one marked file in `rawr run` reveals and lowers only that file again. That now holds when another marked file reads a file with `include_str!` or `include_bytes!`, or a variable with `env!`, as inboard's theme does, and when the edit is to a method's body. With `RAWR_VERBOSE`, the runner says how many files each save revealed.

`rawr test` of a program whose package has Rust dependencies runs its tests in the program's runner, as `rawr run` runs its `main` there, and reports as `cargo test` does. That covers each test's result, a failure's output and panic, libtest's filters and options, the exit status, and `cargo check --profile test`'s errors after the report.

A save that adds or removes a line in a marked file keeps every other marked file's lowering, as long as the line is in a function body or is a blank or comment line. The save lowers only its own file.
A save reads each marked file's outline once per text and keeps it across passes and saves. Before, it blanked every file's text against every body on each pass.

A `Box<dyn Fn>`, a `&dyn Fn` or a `&Box<dyn Fn>` fills a function's `impl Fn` or `F: Fn` input, as in Rust, so a boxed style closure given to iced's `container::style` checks and runs. An `Rc` or `Arc` of one stays an error, as in rustc. Messages name a box or reference of a function `dyn Fn(..)`, and a crate method on a borrowed receiver can call back a closure the receiver holds.
A type alias of an associated type takes its defaulted parameters written, so `fn f() -> canvas::Geometry<Renderer>` checks and runs, as iced's sandpiles writes it.

A crate function's or method's type parameter that only an argument's std-trait bound names is inferred from std's impl for the argument's type, as in rustc. `Link` of iced's `rich_text(spans)` given a `Vec<Span<'static, ()>>`, an array or a slice is `()`, through `AsRef`, `Borrow` and the other std impls.
A crate function a `use` names can be called with a turbofish, as `span::<()>("e")`.
An expression nests and a function recurses as deep as a debug build of Rust allows. There is no expression-depth limit, and the call depth is 100 000.
A spawned thread's panic, and a runner's main panic, name the file, line and column where they panicked.
`collect()` into a `Result` or an `Option` of a map or a set runs.
`rawr test` runs `cargo check` on the tests beside it and reports what only rustc rejects.

A check parses the program once and keeps the parse across its demand rounds, where each round used to parse every source again. `RAWR_VERBOSE=1` also prints, per round, the harnesses bound, build outputs copied, bundles sealed and sources parsed.

A demand round no longer resolves, builds or seals a new bundle when an earlier round built the same crates: it probes the new demand over that build and replays the grown tables. A cold check of a marked theme builds the nightly twice instead of four times.

`RAWR_VERBOSE=1 rawr run` says what preparing the run did: its rounds, Cargo resolutions, nightly builds, probes, runner builds and the units they compiled. A second run of an unchanged project shows all of them at zero.

rawr compiles the dependency versions your Cargo.lock pins. A project without a resolution universe was resolved without its lock and could get newer compatible versions than cargo builds. The runner also no longer warns about a `[patch]` only the rest of your workspace uses.

A project whose Cargo.lock is over 1 MiB resolves from its lock. A crate type's `&'static [&'static str]` const can be read. `Some(&value)` where an `Option<&dyn Trait>` is expected coerces to the trait object, as rustc does. Borrowing a local for a crate's `&'static dyn` field is rustc's E0597 before the run.

A crate whose types nest deeply, such as a long combinator chain, no longer fails `rawr check` with "rawr misread rustc's output (`sidecar-schema`): recursion limit exceeded". The compiler's output also writes each definition id once, which cuts its definitions to about 57% of their former size.

A crate's `use Item as _` of an item that is surely not a trait, such as a module, struct or function, no longer fails the extraction with "rawr misread rustc's output (`anonymous-import-kind`)": as in rustc it adds nothing. A trait's `use Trait as _` still brings its methods into scope, and a declaration whose shape failed closed is refused by name, since it may be a trait.

A save of a marked file in a running `rawr run` no longer does work that grows with the program's dependencies. Each native use finds its binding by one search of an index built when the runner starts, and the owner and the runner parse only the file that changed.
A save of a marked file no longer re-reads, re-encodes or re-stages the running build's native watch: a body edit registers no watcher root.

A method with elided lifetimes whose output borrows its receiver, as `fn user(&self, id: &Id) -> Option<&User>`, can be called from marked code: its lifetimes are read as the call's own, not as a higher-ranked signature. A method that gives `&T` or `Option<&T>` also works on a receiver native code lent, or on a field of one, and may take arguments.

A save that changes a script impl's shape, such as a provided method it now overrides or a signature it changes, now reaches native code. `rawr run` used to swap in the new code while native code kept calling the old shape; the save now rebuilds the runner, and body edits still apply in place.

An expected type reaches every arm of `if`/`else` and `match`, a block-like tail of a block or function body, and every `break` value of a `loop`, and each arm coerces to it as rustc does. `let style: Box<dyn Fn(&Theme) -> Style> = if c { Box::new(|t| ..) } else { Box::new(|t| ..) };` checks, as do `&dyn` and `fn`-pointer arms.
A save of one marked file lowers only that file again; every other file reuses its lowering from the last compile. `RAWR_VERBOSE` says how many files a save lowered.

A check whose first build records new instances of marked generics no longer probes that build, and a check keyed by proved facts proves each imported call in place instead of starting again for each call. A toolchain or driver version mismatch stops a check at once.

An operator on a type without an impl of its trait is rustc's error in rustc's words, at the operator: E0369 for `+`, `|`, `<=` and `==`, E0368 for `+=`, E0600 for unary `-`, and E0308 for a right operand the one impl doesn't take. A `.into()` that nothing fixes is E0283 in every build.
A project's record of native instances is keyed by the rawr build that kept it, and the runner a check builds reads the same key, so a record from an older rawr is never reused.

Marked code calls a crate trait's `&self` methods on a trait object, as `held.0.area()` on a `&'static dyn Shape` or a `Box<dyn Shape>` a crate gave. A marked value is lent to native code as a native trait's `&dyn`, written `&page as &dyn Page` or `&page`, and `Rc<dyn Trait>` and `Arc<dyn Trait>` cross for marked types, numbers and crate values.
`&format_args!(..)` needs no `as &dyn Value` where a crate call takes `&dyn Value`. A slice of objects lent to a call whose result keeps none of them is accepted.
inboard's marked files that name a std trait beside tracing's macros pass `rawr check` again. The extraction error now names the item it misread, not a bare hash.
`-` of an unsigned integer or literal is rustc's E0600 ("unsigned values cannot be negated"), and changing a std collection through a `&` reference is rustc's E0596 in its words.

More std paths run as cargo's build runs them: `std::num::ParseIntError` written in full in a `let`, an imported `Duration` or `Instant` in a `let`, `Instant::now` as a value, `fmt::Formatter::write_str(f, s)`, `Iterator::sum::<i64>(it)`, `<i64 as FromStr>::from_str`, `<T as TryFrom<U>>::try_from`, and `SystemTime`'s `+`, `-`, `+=`, `-=` with a `Duration` and its ordering.
A panic in a project's `main`, sync or async, prints Rust's `thread 'main' panicked:` and its message instead of rawr's internal text.

A frame-held element lends itself to a `&mut Vec<String>` call such as `labels` and to a crate function's `&T`, two values of one opaque type go to one call such as `hover(a, b)`, and `Column::with_children([span(&name), span("right")])` runs again inside a view.
A generic crate trait's method is called by its path with the trait's arguments, as in `Counted::<u8>::doubled(x)`.

A marked module that logs through a crate's re-export of tracing's macros, as inboard's inbox calls its own `log::warn!`, passes `rawr check` and runs as cargo runs it, even when the package names neither tracing nor tracing-core.
Assigning through `&self` is rustc's E0594, and a `&mut self` call through it is rustc's E0596, where rawr gave its own RAWR-RESOLVE-RECEIVER-MUTATION.

A program with marked generic instances keeps its extracted tables for the next demand round again, so a round whose items the tables already hold needs no nightly build or probe. A check no longer generates its bindings plan twice per round, and `rawr check` with `RAWR_VERBOSE=1` prints what each round's stages did.

`std::env::current_dir()` runs, a generic function's type parameter is inferred through an `impl Trait` argument as rustc does, a borrowed crate field derefs at a call even when the program never names its type, and `Rectangle::<u32> { .. }` literals work. iced's screenshot passes `rawr check`, and todos and integration get further.

A crate macro that includes a file relative to a native module, as `wgpu::include_wgsl!("shader/vert.wgsl")`, finds it: a native module's non-`.rs` files sit beside its copy. iced's integration gets past its shaders.
Native code can call a marked generic function at a type that sits below a private module, as inboard's `workspace::spreadsheet` uses its private `sidebar` module's `Message`.

Native code can call a generic marked method or function taking an impl of a marked trait, as inboard's `Sidebar::content(impl IntoContent<'a, Message>)`, with the trait's own type or any iterator of elements. A body edit swaps in place.

A crate function that takes trait objects in a slice, each alone or in an `Option`, and gives back a value that borrows them, as tracing-core's `fields.value_set_all(&[Some(&n as &dyn Value), None])`, runs from marked code. The value can be read, passed to a crate function such as `Event::dispatch(meta, &set)`, or passed to a closure.

A generic marked function's call to another marked generic takes its type arguments from the expected type (a return, `let` annotation, argument or field), as rustc does, so inboard's `Sidebar::default()` in a function returning `Sidebar<'a, Message>` passes `rawr check`. A turbofish no longer counts an argument-position `impl Trait`.

A `Box<dyn Iterator<Item = T>>` that marked code makes, as inboard's sidebar `Header::new` keeps, crosses to native code as an iterator that pulls one item from marked code at each `next`. Native code and marked `&mut self` methods pull from the same iterator.
When `cargo check` also fails, `rawr check` and `rawr run` show cargo's errors alone, with rustc's own text and positions. A supervised run's `failed` event carries rustc's diagnostics.
A marked type boxed as a native trait object works again when the crate's root imports the trait, as with `use page::Page;`. The trait is now compared by the one path it's known by.
A crate's re-exported enum variant reads by its path in marked code, as in `.align_y(iced::Center)` with iced's `pub use Alignment::Center;`.

inboard's sidebar builders run from native code. A marked `&mut self` view passes its lent `Pixels` to a crate call, moves the elements native code keeps into a crate column, and mixes widgets that two crates' paths make in one row. A marked function borrows native code's `&Theme` through the crate root's `pub use` without a clone.

A method taking `self` or `mut self` can move a part below its fields out of the receiver, as in `let items = self.content.items;`, as rustc allows. Behind `&self` or `&mut self` the move is rustc's E0507, naming the place.
A crate trait's function can be called through the trait's module path: `home::Shape::size(&x)`, `crate::home::Shape::size(..)` and `<T as home::Shape>::size(..)` resolve, as in rustc.

`rawr check` on a large workspace joins each loaded crate's artifact to its unit once, walking the build graph once per check instead of once for each crate that loads it. In inboard this was 46% of the check's single-threaded time after an install.
`rawr check` shows which phase it's in on one line, updated in place: resolving, extracting N of M, reading API, classifying, generating, checking.

inboard's sidebar style builders run under `rawr run`. A crate calls marked style closures with the lent `&Theme` without copying it. An `impl Fn(&Theme, Status)` that a native function or `Ternary::with` gives is held boxed. A crate trait with its own `from` in scope no longer breaks the runner.

Real `tracing::warn!("..")` and `info!("..")` events, and `level_enabled!`, run in marked code and reach a native subscriber as cargo's build gives them, also through a crate's re-export, as inboard's `log::warn!` is. `format_args!` is `fmt::Arguments`: its `{:?}` is unquoted, and it coerces to a crate's `&dyn Value`.

`rawr check` classifies a crate's API without re-reading a trait's implementations for every implementation and function that bounds one of its associated types, and finds a type's definition through an index instead of hashing every definition. In inboard's post-bump check this work was about 40% of rawr-import's single-threaded time.
A use of an owned `self`'s field, or of `self`, after a field moved out of it is rustc's E0382. A use after only part of a value moved says "partially moved", as rustc does.
A crate trait's methods work on a std number, `bool` or `char` with the trait in scope, as `count.to_u32()` with num-traits' `NumCast`, and through a qualified path, as `<u64 as NumCast>::from(n)`.
A save near a call to a crate function generic over a const length, as `total([a, b])` is, now swaps into the running program instead of preparing again.

Native code can call a marked function that takes an `impl IntoIterator<Item = T>`, `impl Into<T>`, `impl AsRef<str>` or `impl Display`. The argument may be any value, including one that borrows locals. The program builds as `cargo check` does and runs as `cargo run` does.

When rawr's native build fails in code it generated for a marked function, the error now points at that function's signature in the marked file and names the generated file and line, not just `src/main.rs`.

A program under `rawr run` now goes on from the call that admitted a save only once the run's events include `swapped`. A `wait` that the client cancelled no longer takes the events it found, so the next `wait` returns them.

A `&self` method of a marked type that crosses by copy, such as inboard's `Id::as_str`, now gives native code a `&str` into its own value, as rustc does, instead of panicking. Methods of marked types that hold native parts also return their copied text fields in place.

A marked type's `HashSet`, `HashMap`, `BTreeSet` or `BTreeMap` over values that cross, such as inboard's `read_ids: HashSet<Id>`, now crosses by copy as a `Vec` does. Marked code's `contains`, `insert` and `extend` run on the interpreter's own collection, hashed and compared as Rust does.

A `static` item inside a block or function body now builds, as in `fn place() -> &'static u32 { static PLACE: u32 = 9; &PLACE }`. It is the module's item, as a `static` written there is. A `static` that a macro call expands to is reported as not supported yet, not as a syntax error.

A marked fn taking an `impl` of a trait its own file declares now builds and runs when native code calls it. The trait and its impls are declared natively, and each value is given by the marked impl for its type. Before, the native build failed with E0405.
When the native build fails in the signature of a marked fn that native code can't call yet, the error now names the marked file's line and the word it is at.

A program's blanket impl over a type parameter, such as `impl<T> Trait for T where T: IntoIterator<Item = X>` beside `impl Trait for Content`, now resolves and runs the way rustc selects it. A call on the concrete type runs its own impl. A call on any type the where-clauses hold for, such as a Vec, an array, an iterator or a Display value, runs the blanket impl, directly or through an `impl Trait` bound.
A crate type now compares with another type through its PartialOrd<Rhs> or PartialEq<Rhs>, as tracing's `Level <= LevelFilter::current()` does.
std's macros now work by their paths and through a crate's re-export, as log's `__private_api::module_path!()` and tracing's `__macro_support::concat!` do. `format_args!` is supported.
Native code can now format a marked value it is lent as `&dyn Debug`, `&dyn Display` or another std formatting trait. It also takes `format_args!` as `fmt::Arguments`.

A `static` declared in a marked body, or by a crate macro at each call, is named only in its block. One of a native type is a native value with a fixed `'static` address for the program's life, made the first time its block runs. A save that leaves its declaration alone keeps it, and a save that changes it makes a new one without a restart. Statics that refer to each other, as tracing's `META` and `__CALLSITE` do, are refused at `rawr check` for now.
A crate function that takes a `&'static T` of a native type, or a method that takes `&'static self`, now takes a static's own place. It used to fail the runner build with E0597.

A marked function that native code calls with its own `&str`, and that returns a crate value borrowing it, now builds and keeps native code's own text. inboard's `subtitle<'a>(label: &'a str) -> Text<'a>` is one. It used to fail the native build with "lifetime may not live long enough", because iced's `Text` is invariant in its lifetime. Each `&str` also stops leaking one pinned copy per call.

A marked struct or enum with a lifetime parameter, such as a `Panel<'a>` of `&'a str` and `Element<'a, Message>`s, now crosses to native code. Native code builds one through a chain of marked builder methods, by value and by `&mut`, and keeps it between calls. Its borrows are native code's own.

A bound naming a generic trait the crate declares, with a lifetime among its arguments, now resolves as rustc resolves it. Examples are `impl IntoContent<'a, Message>` on a method of `impl<'a, Message> Sidebar<'a, Message>`, `C: IntoContent<'a, M>`, and a free fn's `impl IntoContent<'a, Message> + 'a`. When such a bound isn't satisfied, rawr writes the trait as rustc does, with `'_` for each lifetime.

Statics declared in a body that refer to each other, as tracing's `META` and `__CALLSITE` do, now work in marked code. Each points at the other, registration by address works, and a save keeps or replaces them without a restart. A cycle whose type keeps the pointer inside an enum or a union is refused at `rawr check`.
`concat!` and other compile-time macros now take a std macro named by a path from the crate root, as in `::core::line!()`.
Native code can call a marked function that is generic over its message, at each type rustc's check saw it called with, directly or through a generic native helper. A body edit to it swaps in place.
A std macro that a crate re-exports and names only inside its own macros, as tracing does with `line!()` inside `concat!`, now resolves in marked code.
A `macro_rules` `expr` fragment no longer starts at its own stop token, so a matcher such as tracing's `fieldset!` matches exactly what rustc matches.

A marked fn whose result's elided lifetime borrows a marked value native code lent it, as `sidebar(theme: &Theme) -> Element<'_, Message>`, can give it on to another marked fn that hands it to native code. The last native call gets native code's own reference instead of panicking.

A marked module of iced builders shaped as inboard's sidebar passes `rawr check` as `cargo check` does. That covers `[4, 0].into()` into a crate type, `impl IntoFragment<'a>` bounds, a blanket program-trait impl calling generic builders, closures annotated `&Theme` through a re-export, `native_fn.with(x)` from a glob-imported trait, a native fn's `impl Fn(&Theme, Status)` given to `style`, and `column(&mut boxed_iterator)`.

Native code can build and keep a marked type generic over its message, as inboard's `Sidebar<'a, Message>`, through its generic methods, and call marked generic functions that take an `impl Trait` argument. A body edit swaps in place.

Marked code builds crate values that hold trait objects, as tracing's `Identifier(&__CALLSITE)`, and holds or passes back a crate's `Box<dyn Trait>`. A number, `bool`, `char` or crate value coerces to a crate trait's `&dyn` or `Box<dyn>`, and the impl for its exact type runs. Native code makes every object.

Two modules of a crate may each declare their own trait of one name, as rustc allows. Each is known by its path, as `home::IntoContent` beside `sidebar::IntoContent`, in bounds, impls, `impl Trait`, `dyn Trait` and calls by the trait's name. A crate trait a module imports with `use` can be implemented by that name.
A marked view can pass a lent value to a crate fn that also takes a `&str`, as in `inbox::view(title, theme).map(..)`, including when the output keeps both the string and the lent value.
A lent value reached at the wrong type is reported as a rawr bug, not as a runtime error in the user's program.

A new engine installs std's declarations as they were written once from the std table, instead of reading the table at every start. That is about 29 ms less per browser instance and 11 ms less per native thread.

A marked function that takes `Option<Element<'a, Message>>` by value from native code, as inboard's `home::State::view` takes `home_grid`, can now call `.map` on the element. Before, a value given this way was checked against the marked theme's native mirror, while `.map` expected the marked type itself, so the call failed. A native value whose type doesn't match what a call expects is now reported as a rawr bug, not as an error in the program.

A marked screen that passes a native function by name, as inboard's `home.rs` passes `theme::text::base` to `.style`, no longer restarts on a body edit above that call; it swaps in place. The runner names the function, not where the program writes it. When a save does need a new native build, `rawr run` says which native input or native use changed instead of "native code changed".

When a save can't compile inside the running program, `rawr run` says why in one line, `rawr: preparing again: <reason>`, and the events stream carries `{"event":"preparing","reason":…}`. The reason is one of: a refresh, the native input that changed since the running build was checked, `Cargo.toml` or what native code sees of the marked modules, an earlier save's pending native build, or the running program's own miss.

A marked fn whose element borrows only native inputs now runs, as `fn view<'a>(threads: &'a Store) -> Element<'a, Message>` does. So does a fn that reads a crate call's output right where it makes it, from values native code lent it.
A lent slice passed beside a lent value to a crate fn that keeps neither now works.

An edit to a marked file that passes a crate function by name to a crate method, as `.style(theme::text::base)` does, now swaps into the running program. It used to take the full preparation on every save: about 2.5 minutes for the first edit on inboard.
A call that passes a closure to a widget held boxed in a view builds, as when iced's modal styles its `center(..)` container. iced's modal runs.

A marked module's path through a `use` that binds a marked module now reaches that module's native children, as rustc does. inboard's `use crate::theme;` followed by `theme::text::base` is an example. A native signature's `&Theme` of a marked theme is now the marked type itself, not a different one. Each crate function item passed to a generic, as in `.style(theme::text::base)` beside `.style(theme::container::base)`, calls its own function. Before, they could share one adapter.

iced's `pane_grid` example runs again. A `&self` method on a crate value generic over the program's own type, such as `self.panes.len()` on a `pane_grid::State<Pane>`, can read it while a view still borrows it, as rustc allows. It no longer stops with a false E0502 before the window opens. This had regressed in #1432.

An `if`, `while`, `for` or `match` missing its `{` now reads as rustc's "expected `{`, found `2`", and nothing follows it. Before, it shifted the braces and surfaced as a `self` error in a later method. A free function's `self` parameter reads as rustc's "`self` parameter is only allowed in associated functions". A `self` value outside a method reads as E0424, replacing RAWR-RESOLVE-SELF.

A marked view that native code lends a marked value to, as inboard's `home::view` gets `theme: &Theme`, can pass it on by `&Theme` to native functions, crate generics and `'a` parameters that its result keeps. Native code gets its own reference back, where it used to panic. A native type alias over a marked type, such as inboard's `Element<'a, Message>`, names the marked type wherever marked code uses it. That removes a false E0308 on `return crate::widget::void();`.

A universe in a browser, such as elevato.rs's page, prepares its bindings about eight times faster: 10.8 s down to about 1.4 s, measured natively. Installing a crate's items now sorts once, instead of shifting the registry for each item. Each item and type that re-exports reach at many paths is stored and converted once. The embedded bindings plan shrinks from 97.6 MB to about 26 MB.

A crate's `&mut self` method now works on a temporary, as in inboard's `rand::rng().random_range(0..100)`. The call's value is borrowed where it is made and lives to the end of its statement, as rustc does. This replaces a RAWR-RESOLVE-HOST-OPERATION "not supported yet" error.

A crate's `&self` or `&mut self` method now reaches an element of a slice that a native method lends where it is. Examples are `entry.is_shared()` in `for entry in registry.entries()`, and on a `Vec<&Entry>` collected from it. It used to panic at run time with "a value reached an adapter as a type its signature doesn't take".

A browser universe prepares about four times faster: elevato's `prepare()` goes from 1.25 s to about 0.29 s, measured natively. A whole-crate or whole-module re-export is now one alias that the runner's registry follows, not a copy of its entries. The facade plan also writes identities as hex. elevato's plan drops from 25.8 MB to 14.8 MB, and its wasm from 51.9 MB to 41.0 MB.

A call inside a crate macro's arguments now runs in Rust's order around a call whose value borrows a local, as in inboard's `stack![page, opaque(wizard.view(catalog, theme).map(..))]`. It used to be refused as "a call or assignment run before a call whose value borrows a local".

A marked view whose scope frame captures values that aren't `Send` or `Sync` now builds under `rawr run`. Examples are a native view of borrows into a type with `RefCell` or `OnceCell` caches, and an owned iced `Element`, as in inboard's `wizard.view(catalog, ..)` and `sidebar::header_row`. Before, the generated runner failed with E0277. A frame's opener stays on the thread that made it. A native value lent to a marked call by `&` or `&mut` no longer has to be `Send` or `Sync`.

Projects now share generated bindings for crates whose build scripts leave native build files, such as openpnp_capture_sys's CMake tree and aws-lc-sys's stray objects. rawr compares only the OUT_DIR files a compile read. `rawr check` reads the project's build-script outputs when its cargo check ends, before another toolchain's build can rerun them. Not sharing names its real reason, and each note prints once. In a fixture, a second project's check went from 10.5 s, not shared, to 4.0 s, shared.

A runner's bindings now load in about a millisecond. Each binding is built the first time a program looks it up, from a binary image the generator writes. elevato's page prepares in under 30 ms in Chrome instead of about 0.7 s, and native runners start the same way.

A marked view can now map the element that a native function returns over a lent marked type, as inboard's `home::State::view` does with `inbox::view(.., theme).map(Message::Inbox)`. It used to fail with "the lent value is not of the type this call takes". A marked type now has one spelling in the runner, so the returned element and the receiver of `map` are the same type.

A package with marked modules builds its native side with its `[features]`, as `cargo run` does: its default features are on, code under `#[cfg(feature = "…")]` builds as under Cargo, and an optional dependency a feature enables is there, inherited from a workspace or not.
A build script that declares modules with `mod`, at `build.rs` or wherever `build` puts it, finds them beside it, nested modules included.
A dependency whose build script isn't named `build.rs` no longer loses its dependency information in rawr's store.
A call through a crate the program doesn't depend on, as `tokio::spawn(..)` without tokio, is rustc's E0433 naming that crate, and a panic in a native async call reaches you as cargo shows it.
A crate whose method returns an `impl Trait`, such as polars-core's `downcast_iter_mut`, no longer crashes rawr-import's driver with a rustc internal error about a missing visibility.

The whole site now has the work plan's look: Abitaro Sans, black on white with one red, heavy headings and thick rules. Every page, /todo included, has a dark mode that follows the system, with a switch in the site bar that remembers the choice.

The playground's examples have a Rustlings group: 13 programs from the rustlings solutions (ownership, enums, Option, strings, HashMap, errors with ? and Box<dyn Error>, traits, lifetimes, iterators, Box, Rc and TryFrom), each crediting its source under rustlings' MIT licence.

A module, its file, a function, a field or a binding can be named `switch`, `import`, `print`, `this` or any other word the old engine reserved, in marked code and in a crate's items, as in Rust: `mod switch;` opens `switch.rs`. rawr's grammar is Rust's, so the old engine's `switch`, `do`/`until`, `try`/`catch` and `import`/`export` syntax is gone.

The landing page's reload section now covers any library: tabs show the same idea in iced, ratatui and a plain std loop, and a new docs page, Apps and libraries, explains how libraries are compiled by Cargo, called from marked code and reloaded on save. Section rules, headings, links and inline code read more evenly.
An `Option` or a `Result` is an iterator of the value it holds: `for x in opt`, `for x in &opt`, `opt.iter()` and `opt.into_iter()` walk it, as std's `IntoIterator` impls do.
Assigning through an `Rc` or an `Arc` is rustc's E0594, "cannot assign to data in an `Arc`".
A formatted value whose type nothing settles is rustc's E0282 at its `let`, such as "type annotations needed for `Vec<_>`".
`assert!()`, `assert_eq!()` and `assert_ne!()` with missing arguments give rustc's own macro errors.
An unknown name inside `thread::spawn`'s closure, or in any std path's arguments, is rustc's E0425 rather than a not-yet error.

A bound such as `T: AsRef<str>` or `T: AsMut<u32>` holds for std's types by std's impls, and `as_ref`, `as_mut`, `borrow`, `borrow_mut` and `deref_mut` run through it, a mutable one changing the value where it is. An array of different functions of one signature holds `fn` pointers.

A type can implement one generic trait more than once: `impl From<&str> for Bar` beside `impl From<String> for Bar`, two `impl Convert<T>` of your own trait, or one trait for both `f32` and `f64`. `Bar::from(x)`, `x.into()`, methods, operators and functions without `self` pick the impl by type, as rustc does, and a call nothing picks an impl for is rustc's E0283.

A build input reached through a symlink, such as a header under the SDK path `xcrun --show-sdk-path` prints, is the file the link resolves to, as for Cargo. Pointing the link elsewhere or editing its target runs the build script again and rebuilds the crate.
The play bot's status page and its invite page now look like the rest of the site, in light and dark themes that follow the system or the site's theme switch.
A program may name its types and modules anything, `Program`, `Error` and `Message` included: the generated runner keeps its own items in a module no program names.
A marked `src/main.rs` names its package's library by the crate name, as a Cargo binary does: the library is built, read and bound like any dependency.
A crate function whose `impl Trait` output captures a parameter a closure fills, such as iced's `markdown::code_block`, no longer panics rawr-import when a member of that output is called.

The site's Run buttons run snippets in your browser, as the playground does, with no server round trip and no browser check after an edit. The landing page runs its hello program and a bouncing-ball loop, and the borrow-checking examples in How it works run and show their errors. A few blocks that need what the browser lacks (threads, the clock, wide integers) still run on rawr's server and say so. The site bar is plain at the top of the page and takes a light shade and a hairline once the page scrolls.
A widget moved into a `row!` in one branch and a `column!` in the other runs: each container's methods are that container's own. iced's progress_bar runs.
A view closure that captures nothing and takes a crate value native code lends it, as `transition`'s `|animation, at| ..`, runs: the value is lent for that call.
iced's lazy runs: the widgets its closure makes are `'static`, and a string literal they take outside the view, as `button("Delete")`, is a `&'static str`.
A program's impl of a crate's generic method passes a value of a parameter's associated type from one call to the next, as `painter.fits(painter.font())`.
Two default methods of one trait that give opaque types, as `explain` and `outlined` of one extension trait, each have the members of their own type.

An idle app under `rawr run`, such as a paused simulation or a window waiting for events, is no longer stopped after a few minutes with "the runner did not finish a frame before its deadline". The owner waits for the runner's reply for as long as the runner lives.

A program under `rawr run` can tell it is and hears what each save did. `RAWR_RELOAD_EVENTS` names a socket that carries one JSON event per line: `restarted` first in a process a save restarted, then `queued`, `swapped`, `failed` with its message, file, line and column, and `restarting` with its reason. Under cargo the variable is absent. The new dependency-free `rawr-reload` crate reads it: `rawr_reload::outcomes()` gives each `Outcome` as it comes, and is `None` outside `rawr run`.

The old engine is gone from rawr: try/catch, do/until loops, import/export and the module resolvers, custom syntax and operators, and the old built-ins (type_of, is_shared, is_def_var, is_def_fn, eval, Fn). The lexer reads ?., ?[, ??, !in, ===, !==, := and :; as rustc does, and code writing them gets rustc errors such as "invalid comparison operator `===`" and "keyword `catch` cannot follow a `try` block". The reserved words are exactly Rust own.

A crate's `impl Iterator<Item = T>`, given by a function or a type's method, is an iterator: `next()`, `for` and the iterator's adaptors pull from it. A type's method that gives an `impl Trait` has the trait's methods.
A snippet of top-level statements drops its locals at its end, in reverse order, as `fn main` does, natively and in the browser.
In the browser, `u128` and `i128` values print, compare and do arithmetic as they do natively, instead of printing their type names.

In the browser, `Instant` and `SystemTime` read the page's clock instead of stopping rawr. If rawr itself stops on a program, that program runs on the server and the next run loads a fresh copy of rawr.
A playground snippet that opens with an inner attribute such as `#![allow(dead_code)]` runs as a file, as `rawr run` runs it.

A marked module inside an existing app names the items of its native crate root as rustc lets a child module: `crate::Message::Page(..)`, `use crate::Message;`, `super::helper()`, the root's constants, aliases and `use` re-exports. rawr's copy of the crate makes the root's own items public, and your files stay as they are.

A workspace whose path or Git package has a build script that prints no rerun-if line now checks and runs: rawr watches that package's whole directory (all but its .git, its target and nested packages), so a second run replays and an edit to any file there runs the script again, as under `cargo run`. A staged API table left by a failed run is rechecked against that directory too.

A widget made of what a view borrows can be wrapped by crate functions that give `impl Widget` and by types that hold one, as iced's modal does with `opaque(mouse_area(center(opaque(content))))` and pane_grid with `Content<'a, .., impl Widget>`. Methods and crate functions that take it first work, including ones that take another of the view's widgets. Your own impl of a crate trait can be used at a type of yours that holds a crate's `impl Trait` value, as loupe's `impl Widget for Loupe<W>`: `rawr check` accepts it and the runner builds it.
A generic function of yours that names a crate type takes the type parameter a later use of its value fixes, as rustc infers it: iced tour's `padded_button("Back").on_press(..)` fixes `Message`.
A crate impl's bound that names an associated type fixes a type argument, as rustc's projection does: iced's `image("ferris.png")` takes the renderer's `image::Handle`, so ferris's runner builds.
A function written `-> impl Widget<Message>` gives a crate bound on its output the trait's default renderer, as rustc does, so url_handler runs.
The runner names the type of a native value it takes from a call's arguments, so delineate's runner builds.

Rust code on the site and in the playground is highlighted in nine classes (keywords, types, functions and macros, strings, numbers, escapes, attributes and lifetimes, comments, doc comments), with a palette that meets 4.5:1 in light and dark. Static blocks, Run blocks and the editor share one grammar and one mapping.
`rawr run` of a program that ends while a save is being prepared ends with the program's own exit status, instead of exiting 1 with a framework error that said the save failed.

The site, the playground and the bot share a new favicon: a red disc over a heavy rule, with a red triangle for the playground and the bot, following the browser's light or dark theme. The link previews for the site, /todo and the bot's invite are redrawn in the site's black, white and red with that mark, and each preview's URL carries its content hash so chat apps fetch the new card. The build progress bar draws in the site's reds instead of pink.

A marked function can give native code back a value of a native type: the app's own `Message`, a struct from `main.rs`, or another crate's type. It works bare, inside an `Option`, a `Vec`, a tuple or a `Result`, and for a type with a lifetime such as `iced::Element<'a, Message>`. Native code gets the value itself.

Native code can pass a marked function a native value by value, and the function keeps it as Rust would. A `&mut` native value the function changes, or replaces with `*value = new`, comes back changed. `item.count += 1` on another crate's struct field works, and `item.name.push('!')` on its `String` field changes the struct instead of a copy.

A plain http request to the site, the playground or the bot pages moves to the same URL on https (301 for a GET, 308 for a POST so a playground request stays a POST). Before, http served the page as is.

rawr puts no time limit of its own on anything. The runner protocol waits for the runner as long as it lives. The `rawr mcp` tools take no `timeout_ms` or `wait_ms`: `start` answers once the program runs, `check` once it has checked, `wait` at the next event, `step` where it paused; `break` and `continue` answer at once and `wait` tells the pause. A client that bounds its calls cancels them.
rawr no longer forgets an installed rawr-import: a manifest probe that fails, as one could under heavy load, is asked again on the next run instead of being remembered as 'not installed'.

A crate type whose impls at different arguments each have a method of one name giving an `impl Trait`, as swash's `Setting<u16>` and `Setting<f32>` do with `parse_list`, imports again, so iced's examples that draw text check.
The landing page is shorter: each example shows its code, its command and its output, and the bouncing ball is drawn across the page.

A value of yours that holds one of a view's values, as iced's loupe holds what `explain` gives of its `column![..]`, is reached after the view returns: the view's values live as long as the state the view borrows stays unchanged.

Your impl of a crate's trait at a type that holds a crate's opaque value can delegate to it, as `self.content.labels(labels)` or `Widget::press(&self.content, label)`: a `&mut Vec<String>` the crate lent your method reaches the crate's own vector.

iced's pane_grid runs: a closure that gives a value at its call's own lifetime, as `PaneGrid::new(&state, |id, pane, max| Content<'a, ..>)` does, makes it in a region of its own at that lifetime, and `content.title_bar(title_bar)` joins values of that region.

A crate whose generic type's impls each give an opaque iterator by one name, as swash's `Setting<u16>::parse_list` and `Setting<f32>::parse_list`, imports: every iced program that draws text checks again.

A function written `-> impl Widget<Message>` or `-> Option<impl Widget<Message>>` fixes its renderer before an `impl Into<Handle>` argument's own type would fix the handle, as rustc does, so gallery's images take iced's `image::Handle` and gallery passes `rawr check`. A crate's opaque widget whose trait names a `String`, as `markdown::view`'s `impl Widget<Uri, ..>`, takes the renderer a later use gives it.

rawr runs a package's binaries as Cargo lists them: one under src/bin/ or named by [[bin]], and a library runs from whichever binary cargo run would run. With several binaries and no default-run, rawr asks for --bin, as cargo run does.

`rawr run path/to/file.rs` runs a file its package lists as a binary as that package's binary, with its dependencies and profile, and `rawr run --bin NAME` (and check and test) picks one as cargo run --bin does. A file no package lists still runs alone.
A package's `panic = "abort"` profile aborts a panic, as the binary Cargo builds does: status 134.
A [target.'cfg(..)'.dependencies] table joins a program's dependencies when Cargo's own build links it on the host. rawr asks Cargo's unit graph and evaluates no cfg itself.
A large project is never refused for its size: the semantic API, the node store, the extraction driver and the attempt record no longer have byte or count caps.

Each runnable snippet on the site had a hand-written output that nothing checked. One error showed only its first line, six compile errors were not marked as errors, and the drop-order output showed what Rust prints rather than what rawr prints. The site's build now runs every snippet in rawr-web, or on the server through /play/render for the three blocks marked data-where="server", and draws each output with the same function the Run button uses (site/src/lib/output.ts). A hand-written output fails the build. /play/render skips Turnstile for the smoke token, and the deploy's smoke test checks each server block's output against the deployed server.

The reference pages were checked claim by claim against the current rawr: overview, requirements, iced, std, closures, generics, items, moves, play and commands. These were stale: gaps that now run (serde derives, crate functions taking your type, async without a runtime, try_join! and select!, consts captured in format strings, entry borrows, std::fs, char::from_u32), a removed difference (the index panic's column), lenient cases rustc's errors now catch (HashMap without use, a field returned by value), a Send bound said to go unchecked, the &dyn gap (it is std traits' trait objects), and quoted errors rawr no longer gives (unknown import, RwLock's not-yet message). Requirements lists rawr-reload, and commands gives exit status 134 under panic = "abort" and the default-run rule. Merged as e94629ca8.

Calling a macro without `!`, as in `print("hi")`, `vec(1)` or `std::print("hi")`, now gives rustc's E0423 "expected function, found macro" with the help "use `!` to invoke the macro". It used to say rawr doesn't run it yet.

docs/reference/iced said what rawr doesn't do for iced (nothing hand-written, nothing prebuilt) and listed gaps such as 'a #[widget] written in a marked file', an attribute that exists nowhere. The page is deleted; /docs/reference/iced redirects to /docs/iced, its bindings and gaps anchors go to Imports, its examples anchor to the iced guide, and the values-cross-both-ways and one-iced-per-project facts stay in Imports and Run.

A marked crate's `cfg!(feature = "..")`, `#[cfg(feature = "..")]` and `#[cfg_attr(..)]` follow the features Cargo enables for it, and `rawr run`, `rawr check` and `rawr test` take `--features`, `--no-default-features` and `--all-features` as `cargo run` does.

A message that a closure gives on iced's executor thread, such as `keyboard::listen().filter_map(..)`'s `Some(Message::SplitFocused(Axis::Vertical))`, keeps the crate values it holds. pane_grid's hotkeys no longer panic.
A crate function returning `impl Trait`, where the trait has a supertrait like `Add<Output = Self>` (as num-traits' `Num` does), now imports. Before, rawr-import overflowed its stack on it.
A method of an opaque output that gives another opaque output of the same method, as `explain(..).explain(..)` does, can be used again. The fix for #1262 had left it unusable at `rawr check`.
A marked module names a native module's trait by path (`Box<dyn page::Page>`, `use crate::page::Page;`) and takes, keeps and returns its objects.
A path into a dependency none of whose items rawr can use yet names the item and says why, as it does for a crate with other items, instead of rustc's "cannot find module or crate".
A crate's function that gives a thread's `JoinHandle`, as `open::that_in_background` does, runs: the program can ignore the handle or `.join()` it for what the thread gave.

A marked crate with Rust dependencies follows Cargo's features: `cfg(feature)` in marked code and in native modules holds as under `cargo run`, with `--features`, `--no-default-features` and `--all-features`.

A crate whose generic trait has a provided method giving an opaque type, where that type's supertrait binds an associated type to Self (as `Add<Output = Self>` does), no longer panics rawr check while building its API. An item whose signature names another item's type parameter is left out with a can't-be-used-yet note.

A std trait works as a trait object, as in Rust. `Box<dyn Error>` with `?` from `parse`, `&dyn Debug` of a derived or builtin value, `&dyn Display` of the program's own impl, and `Vec<Box<dyn Display>>` of mixed values all work, with no `impl Error` needed in the program. Formatting, `to_string()` and the trait's methods call the value's own impl.

A `match` that misses values reports rustc's E0004 in rustc's words: the patterns not covered (`Message::Decrement`, `None`, `i32::MIN..=0_i32` and `2_i32..=i32::MAX`, `&_`), the label on the scrutinee, the matched type and the arm to add. Integer and `char` arms whose ranges cover the whole type no longer need a `_`.

A marked module builds a native module's structs and enums whose fields are `&'static str`, `Option<&'static str>` and `&'static [T]` from literals, and a marked `pub static` of them is compiled natively, so native code reads it as a Rust item.

An array or `vec!` literal's elements coerce to the trait object a parameter, a `let` or a function's return type expects: `all(&[&A, &B])` for `&[&dyn Named]`, and `vec![Box::new(A), Box::new(B)]` returned as `Vec<Box<dyn Named>>`.
A refutable pattern in a `let`, a `for` loop or a function argument is rustc's E0005, naming the values it misses and suggesting `let else` or `if let`.

Importing a crate no longer panics when a type in an item's values form, a type's fields, an alias, a default, a trait or impl header, a relation or an application names a type parameter its declaration doesn't have. One walker (undeclared_parameter in src/package/import.rs) checks everything the build converts for an item; the item is left out with the usual can't-be-used-yet note, and RAWR_VERBOSE=1 prints one line naming the crate, the item, the parameter index, the declared parameter count and the type. The second shape behind #1278 is found with that line on the reporting workspace.

A type alias from a native module, such as `type Width = usize`, now crosses a marked function's signature as its target does: by value, by `&` and as a result. Native code calling the function no longer fails with `Function not found`.

A marked type that implements one of your crate's native traits becomes its object: `Box::new(BadgePage { .. })` gives a `Box<dyn page::Page>` that native code keeps and calls. `&mut self` changes stay for the next call, and a saved method body takes effect at the next call.

A `let` with `ref mut` and a refutable part, a slice pattern on a slice of unknown length, a native struct pattern with refutable fields, and an enum variant in a function parameter are rustc's E0005, with rustc's witnesses. Their irrefutable forms (`let [all @ ..] = s;`, `fn f(One::Only(x): One)`) now run.

A tuple variant or tuple struct pattern with the wrong number of fields is rustc's E0023 (`this pattern has 1 field, but the corresponding tuple variant has 2 fields`), with the declared fields marked and rustc's help to add `_` or wrap the fields in parentheses.

A marked function's `&mut` parameter whose type is a native alias of a plain type, such as `&mut Width` for `type Width = usize`, now crosses as `&mut usize` does. Native callers see the change after the call. A `&mut` of a native type is still lent.

`rawr check` no longer stalls after reading parse cells on an app over iced: a type from another crate's facade is named by that facade's fingerprint, never by re-walking that facade's contract at each mention.

A native trait with supertraits works as a marked type's trait object: `Debug`, `Display`, `Clone`, `PartialEq`, `Eq`, `Hash`, `Default`, `PartialOrd` and `Ord`, derived or written, run the marked type's own impl, and a supertrait the type lacks is rustc's E0277.
A `&self` method of a marked type's native trait object can call back into the same object through native code: `&self` calls share the value, as shared borrows do.

A crate's impl with a `Future<Output = T>` bound is no longer left out when another future's `Output` names a parameter only its where clause fixes. futures_util's forwarding impls for `TakeWhile`, `Fold`, `PollImmediate` and the `&mut`/`Pin`/`Box` blankets are declared now.

Marked code reads a marked `pub static` of native values, such as a page's `BLOCKS: &[page::Block]`, where native code holds it. It reads the length, indexes, iterates, matches, and reads a block's `children`, with no copy. `&BLOCKS[1..2]` lends a range of it to a native function.

A crate's unit struct is a value, as `badge::Secondary` is, through a module or a re-export: it is passed where a method takes `impl Into<T>` through the crate's `From`, compared, printed and matched as a pattern. A tuple struct's constructor is a function value, as in `.map(Wrap)`.

A native trait's `&self` method can return a borrow of the marked value, as `fn label(&self) -> &str` or `fn items(&self) -> &[String]`; native code reads it after the call, and calling a `&mut self` method while it is still in use is rustc's E0502, as under cargo.
`rawr check` on a marked type that lacks a native trait's supertrait shows only cargo's error at the program's own paths, not a failed build of rawr's copy of the crate with generated names.

A `&mut` that a crate method returns, such as image's `get_pixel_mut(x, y)`, is a place: `.0 = v`, `*p = v`, `.0[3] += 1` and passing it on to another crate call change the crate's own value, as in Rust.

`use m::badge::{self, badge};` binds the module and the function of one name, as Rust does: `badge::Secondary` goes through the module and `badge("..")` calls the function. Two `use` lines and a glob beside the module's import do the same. Two imports of one name in one namespace are rustc's E0252.

A crate macro that converts its children with `Into::<Slot<'_, _>>::into(child)`, as a component crate's `badge!` and `row!` do, now takes a string literal through the crate's `From<&'a str>` and a `String` through its `From<String>`, as cargo does. So do `"x".into()`, `From::from("x")` and `<T as From<_>>::from(..)` wherever the target type is known.

`rawr run` of a program that rustc rejects, such as a marked type missing a native trait's supertrait, now shows only `cargo check`'s error, at the program's own paths, without rawr's report of its copy of the crate. A save that breaks the program the same way shows cargo's error too.
A `&mut` a crate method returns is held for its statement or binding, as Rust holds it: `buffer.get_mut(i).0 = v` and `let p = buffer.get_mut(i);` call the method once, not once per access.

A call can take borrowed crate values from several `let`s at once, as `Row::with_children([a, b])` takes two `Slot`s each made from its own string: its output lives as long as the shortest borrow, as in Rust.

`#[cfg(..)]` and `#[cfg_attr(..)]` on a struct expression's field, a match arm, an array or tuple element or a call argument leave it out where they don't hold, as in rustc. This covers crate structs such as iced's `window::Settings { #[cfg(target_os = "macos")] platform_specific: .., ..Default::default() }`. `target_os`, `unix`, `debug_assertions` and every other cfg follow `rustc --print cfg` for the target and profile Cargo builds with.

A crate function's array types work as in Rust: `[T; N]` by value with a const-generic `N` taken from the array you pass (`Row::with_children([a, b])`), `&[T; N]`, `&mut [T; N]` whose writes reach your array or a crate struct's field (`fill(&mut pixel.0, 7)`), and `-> [u8; 4]` results.

A crate macro's children convert through the crate's From impl for their own full type, as rustc selects it: a widget crate's generic Text whose theme only the impl fixes, the crate's own builders, a program's own From impl, and a type reached through a re-export. A child no impl takes gets rustc's E0277 with the types the impls take, never "unknown member".

A crate method's `&mut` of a value a scope frame's region holds, and an `Option<&mut T>` a crate method returns (as pane_grid's `state.get_mut(pane)`), are now called once and held for the statement or binding, as rustc holds them. Such methods are now places whatever their other inputs are.
A program's unit struct named by a module path is its value in a `match` scrutinee and an `if let` value too, as `match badge::Secondary { badge::Secondary => .. }`.

A program's generic `impl<'a, M> From<Mine> for Slot<'a, M>` of a crate type can pass its own `M` to the crate in its body: the impl is compiled for each type its conversions take, as rustc monomorphises it.
A leading `self::` in a path names the current module, as rustc reads it: in values, calls, patterns, types, `use` lists and `self::super::`. `self` after a path's first segment is rustc's E0433.

A native crate root's `mod` declarations are read under the `cfg`s Cargo builds the package with for this target, `cfg_attr` included: `#[cfg(windows)] mod x;` on macOS is no longer scanned, loaded or built, and a `#[path]` applied by `#[cfg_attr(..)]` resolves as rustc resolves it.
A single-file program names its own items through `crate::`, `self::` and `super::` as rustc does, in types, values, calls, patterns and `use`, with rustc's error for `super::` at the root.
`pub use` of an enum variant, by name or by glob, re-exports it from its module, for the program's enums and a crate's.

`rawr run` watches the program's inputs, not the project tree: nothing under `target/` reaches the file watcher, so rawr's own builds no longer count as saves, and a project with a huge `target/` starts its watcher. If macOS refuses the watcher's stream, the error says so and lists the paths rawr asked for.

`clock.strftime("%H:%M")` fills `F: ?Sized` with the unsized `str`; instance_surface_type had no case for that type, so the call carried no instance key and fell back to the item's shared binding, the adapter of whichever instance registered first, in an order set by hashes. New crates in the crate-shapes fixture flipped that order and the literal reached the `[u8]` adapter: the 'a value reached an adapter as a type its signature doesn't take' panic, deterministic in one lane and absent in another, which is also the shape of the #1087 flake. Ty::UnsizedStr now keys as Builtin::Str, as the adapter generator names it. Merged in 1777280a7.

A call of a crate's generic item always reaches the adapter of its own instance. A parameter an associated type reads no longer misses its adapter, and a type argument that keys no instance is a check error at the call, never a call into another instance's adapter at run time.

A marked type behind a native trait object lends its strings in place: `fn label(&self) -> &str` reads the program's own text with no copy, and a `&self` method returning a native type that borrows the value, as `view(&self) -> Element<'_, Message>` does, works and keeps what it borrows only to the next `&mut self` call.
Two `let`s of a crate value that borrows what it takes, such as an invariant `Text<'a>` or what `explain` gives, go to one call outside a view too, as Rust infers one lifetime for both.

rawr keeps one copy of each crate's bindings: the home's for a shared crate, target/rawr/bindings for a path crate, and the file the nightly compiler wrote for bindings that haven't settled. target/rawr/staged holds only a small record for each, keeps those of the last four resolutions that ran the nightly compiler, and drops the rest. A check whose bindings are unchanged writes none of them again.

The iced tab is iced's counter, and Run shows its window's first frame. The ratatui tab draws a to-do screen with ratatui's widgets and prints it as text. Both carry a Run button and the server marker, and the build shows what the server returns. The server's universe gains ratatui 0.30 (play/universe). A block that needs the server's next image (`data-image="next"`) says so while that image isn't live; the ratatui block carries it and its real output appears once the release workflow rebuilds the image and the site builds again. Merged as 7777bd005.

A project's target/rawr now grows by an edit's changes, not by a full copy per edit. The API, generic contract, facade, overlay and a runner's generated sources are kept as shared parts in target/rawr/store.parts, so a new generation writes only the parts it changed. When a runner leaves the four the project keeps, the units only its generation used go with it, and so does every part nothing lists any more. An undo to any of the four newest generations still rebuilds nothing.

Shared bindings and trait facts are kept in one directory per extraction protocol in rawr's home (`formats/<protocol>`). Each directory records the installed rawr executables that use it. An older protocol's directory is removed once it has gone a day unused and no installed rawr uses it, so a protocol bump no longer leaves gigabytes of unreachable entries. `rawr cache clean` now also removes idle shared trait facts, and the home's stale `digests` file is removed.

The docs are grouped as Get started, Guides, Reference and Tools. On desktop they show a sidebar tree; on phones a drawer opens from the bar's Docs control. Every page has breadcrumbs, and every heading on the site links to its own anchor. /docs opens with four reader paths. The iced, iced reload and ratatui pages are now worked examples in Apps and libraries, rewritten as plain documentation, and previews moved to Tools as Editor previews. Old docs URLs no longer redirect.

A push to main that changes `play/universe`, the bot's code or `play/Dockerfile` builds the ?play image and deploys it by itself. A snippet on the site that needs a crate the universe gained no longer waits for the release workflow. Every other change to the site or the docs deploys on push, as before.

`rawr run` starts its file watcher on apps with a thousand dependencies: the OS watches the project's source directories, each path dependency's and each manifest's directory, never every dependency file, and registry and git dependencies get no watch, since a changed one arrives through `Cargo.lock`.
Installing a contract counted its facade roots by rescanning every prior outcome for each outcome, which took minutes on a workspace of a thousand packages. The roots are collected once.
`#[widget]` / `#[rawr::widget]` is gone from rawr-macros and from rawr's parser. It did nothing; `#[preview]` is the one Rawr attribute.

A string literal passed to a crate call that borrows it, as `badge![icon(), "Verified"]` or `Slot::from("x")` does, is `'static` text, as in Rust: no scope frame opens for it, so nested view code such as `row![badge![..].style(..), ..].spacing(8).into()` checks and runs as cargo runs it.

A long-running rawr (such as `rawr mcp`) no longer loses its host directory when another rawr prunes old hosts. Each process leases its host for as long as it runs, and prune and `rawr cache clean` skip leased hosts.

The landing page gets its snippets ready once it has loaded: it fetches rawr-web and runs each snippet in the background. Run then shows the result at once instead of waiting for the download or the server.
The site's Run strips no longer say where a snippet runs: the "on rawr's server" label is gone from the landing page and the docs.

A `use` or path whose crate isn't a dependency now reads as rustc's E0433, with rustc's `cargo add` help. A missing item or module in a present module reads as rustc's E0432 or E0425, with rustc's labels. The help "isn't available in Rawr yet" is gone.

`rawr cache warm` builds what the first run with dependencies used to build: it installs the nightly rawr reads crate APIs with (the one the current directory names, or the pinned one), gets that nightly's driver and std table, and compiles rawr's runtime for your Rust compiler. It prints the same progress lines, or one line when everything is built. The installer runs it, so a fresh install's first `rawr run` no longer stops to compile rawr's runtime.

A crate value's `.into()` whose target type is known but has open arguments, as `Slot<'_, _>` in a row whose message type only a later child fixes, picks the one `From` impl that fits, as rustc does, instead of reporting E0283.

A crate's `From<String>`, `From<&str>` and `From<Cow<str>>` impls stay three: a `String` reaches `From<String>`, a literal `From<&str>`, and only a program's own `Cow<str>` (`Cow::Borrowed`, `Cow::from`) reaches `From<Cow<str>>`, as rustc selects them. Before, a `String` could reach the crate's Cow impl.

A crate value passed to `impl Into<T>` where it already is a `T`, as a component crate's `badge!` passes its `Slot::new(row)` to `badge(content: impl Into<Slot<'a, Message>>)`, takes the target's type arguments, so a later use fixes the row's message as rustc does. A crate value whose type nothing settles is rustc's E0282 at its `let` instead of a runner cargo refuses.

A crate that calls your function with a `&` or `&mut` of its own value, as a simulation's `update(&mut self, message, building: &Building)` does, lends you that value for the call: its type needs no `Clone`, nothing is copied, and each call sees the value as the crate holds it then. Its methods, its fields, `{}`, `{:?}` and `==` reach it where it is, and you can pass it on to the crate's functions that take `&Building`, as a view's `draw(building)` does.

The ?play universe runner builds again: a widget made from a borrowed `&str`, as iced's `button(label)` gives a `Button<'_, Message, &str>`, no longer fails E0597 in its generated adapter, and the generated runner compiles without warnings.

Running one workspace member after another no longer fails with E0463 ("can't find crate for `rawr`"). Each member's runner is now its own Cargo unit in the workspace's build directory, so one member never reuses another member's build script and the shared runtime it names.

`rawr::universe` loads a marked file against a binary's linked generated bindings and runs it in that process. `call(name, args)` or `run()` executes it, and `reload()` or `replace(text)` on any thread reports unchanged, queued, swapped, failed or restarting. ?play's universe runner serves its snippets through it.
`write!` with no `Write` trait in scope is rustc's E0599 "cannot write into `String`", with its help naming `use std::fmt::Write;`.
A `use` inside a block is in scope in that block alone; outside it its names are rustc's E0425.
A bare value where a `Box<dyn Error>` is expected is rustc's E0308, with rustc's `Box::new` or `Into::into` help.
An unsuffixed literal that several `From` impls fit takes rustc's fallback type, i32 or f64, and selects that impl.
An index past a slice's end panics at the expression's start, as rustc places it.
Integer division and remainder by zero or overflow, out-of-range slice ranges, `pow` overflow and a reversed `clamp` panic in rustc's words and at rustc's position.
A project whose `.cargo/config.toml` sets `build.target` (or that runs with `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET`) is read, extracted and generated for that target, as Cargo builds it, such as wasm32-unknown-unknown.

A crate value generic over a program's types can call a script function it kept, such as elevato's `Simulation::frame` calling the program's `update`, and that function can make crate values like a `Task` and give them back. Before, the program panicked with `Stale`.

A view whose message type only its declared return type fixes, as `fn view(..) -> Slot<'static, Message> { match id { .. => row![badge![..].style(..)].into() } }`, runs instead of failing with E0282 at the badge when the crate's Slot is also an Element. A crate type with `From` impls for several generic targets, as a badge that is both a Slot and an Element, converts with `.into()` instead of failing at start with "the bindings have no item".

A function bounded by a trait with more than 64 impls, such as icedxdy's `badge(content: impl Into<Slot<'a, Message>>)`, now ties its argument's types to the callee's, so `badge![icon, "Verified"]` no longer reports E0282.

A native function that keeps the blocks it is given, such as `State::new(page_index, blocks: &'static [Block])`, takes a marked module's `static BLOCKS`, a range of it, or a slice literal, as Rust does. Before, the generated runner failed to compile with E0713/E0521.

A marked type that native code holds as a `Box<dyn Trait>` can return references: a `&'static Meta` or `&'static [Block]` that is a static gives native code the static itself, and `&self.state` is lent where the value holds it. A reference result rawr can't give yet is an error at `rawr check` instead of a panic at the call.

A marked type that native code holds as a `Box<dyn Trait>` can clone a field of a value it lent in place, as `fn scrollable_id(&self) -> Id { self.state.scrollable_id.clone() }` does while native code still holds `&State` from `state()` or a view from `preview()`. icedxdy's browser no longer exits when a page is selected.
A local array or slice borrowed where a crate takes `&'static [T]` is now rustc's E0597, as a borrowed string already was; statics, ranges of them and constant literals still pass.
An unused `use crate::module;` in a marked file is no longer refused with E0432; as in rustc, it is at most a warning.

?play's universe (iced, tokio and ratatui with their generated bindings) builds for wasm32, and the site can run an iced snippet in your browser on it: each Run gets a fresh instance in a frame of its own, drawn by iced's web shell, answering clicks with no round trip to the server. The landing page keeps its iced counter on the server for now, since the browser draws it at the wrong scale on high-density displays.
The landing page's iced counter runs in your browser, in a frame of its own, at any display scale, answering clicks with no round trip to the server.

A method a crate's trait gives another crate's type by a generic impl now resolves, as ratzilla's `WebRenderer` gives ratatui's `Terminal` its `on_key_event`; a block that ends in a closure passed to a crate keeps the closure's parameter types and captures.
`?` converts a crate's error through the crate's `impl From<Error> for io::Error`, and a crate error with a written or derived (thiserror) `std::error::Error` impl boxes as a `Box<dyn Error>`.

When one definition is read under two names of the same toolchain, as `nightly` and the dated nightly it resolves to, rawr treats it as one definition instead of failing with `conflicting-definition`; that error also names the item and both sources.
A crate whose `lazy_static!` declares a hidden struct beside a static of the same name, as `colored`'s `SHOULD_COLORIZE` does, imports instead of failing as declared twice.
A crate that re-exports `core` under another name, as bytemuck's `pub use ::core as __core;`, registers its bindings instead of failing at a module with no parent.

A marked function that native code calls on another thread, as an iced app's `Task::perform` output closure runs on a tokio worker, makes and uses crate values as it does on the main thread, instead of failing with `Stale`.

The playground deploys again: the browser's universe ships as a 5 MB brotli-compressed module that the browser decompresses as it downloads, since the 53 MB raw module was over Cloudflare's limit on one file.

A marked file can define a type over a native one, as inboard's `theme.rs` does with `enum Theme { Selected(themedef::Theme) }`. Its values cross with their native parts, and every impl native code relies on stays: `From` in both directions with native and crate types, a crate trait's impl, and `impl From<&Theme> for markdown::Settings`.
In ?play, a snippet's statements outside `fn main` can call std's path, io, time and fs items again, as the std page's `PathBuf` example does.

rawr checks a project built for another target, such as wasm32, when a dependency's build script uses a build-dependency with host-only dependencies. Before, it stopped with an internal error that a Cargo unit's package was absent from metadata.

Any file in a native crate's module tree can be marked with `// rawr`, not only one declared by the crate root or a marked module. Marked code there reaches its parent's private items, its siblings and its native children as rustc allows, and native code calls into it.

A marked type over a native one, as inboard's `enum Theme { Selected(themedef::Theme) }`, lends its native part to the interpreter where it is when native code borrows it, `&mut self` too, and moves it for a value: no clone, and a part that isn't `Clone` crosses.

A marked type's `&self` method returning a reference into its native part, as `fn colors(&self) -> &Colors`, gives native code that reference where the part is, and marked code can call it as `self.colors().accent`. A `&str` result such as `iced::theme::Base::name` works too.

Slices and `Vec`s run `binary_search`, `binary_search_by`, `binary_search_by_key` and `partition_point` by std's own loop, so each `Ok` among equal elements and each `Err` insertion point is the one rustc's build gives.

A marked module reads a native crate's `const` or `static` of `&str` as `&'static str` and passes it to a crate function that takes one, such as `Font::new(fonts::UI_FAMILY)`, keeping one string for the program's life. A constant of a slice of numbers reads as `&[T]`, as in Rust. An item a module can't give yet is now rustc's E0425 for the module.
A `match` on a marked enum whose variant holds a crate enum (`Message::Wizard(wizard::Message::Step(step))`) is exhaustive where rustc's is, instead of a false E0004.

Native code can keep a marked `State` between calls and poll the `Task<Message>` a marked `update` returns, mapped with a marked variant such as `Message::Wizard`: the task and element types are native code's own.

A marked type can hold a native value that isn't `Clone` inside an `Option`, a `Vec`, a `Box` or a tuple, as inboard's `home::State` holds `wizard: Option<wizard::State>`. Native code lends the value to marked methods where it is, so `self.wizard = Some(..)`, `self.wizard = None`, `self.tabs.push(..)` and `self.tabs.remove(i)` work as in Rust.
A marked function that returns `()` gives native code `()` even when its last statement leaves a value, such as the native part `self.tabs.remove(index);` removes. That case used to fail with E0515.

A save to a program with a native `main` and an idle window loop now shows at once on macOS. rawr asks the program's windows to redraw when it queues a save, so the next frame takes it with no input. Before, the save waited for the next pointer or key event.

Native code can hold the `Element<'a, Message>` that a marked `view<'a>(&'a self, ..)` or `view(&State) -> Element<'_, Message>` returns while it borrows the state. The element's borrowed text lives as long as Rust says it does, and `.map(Message::Wizard)` on such an element works inside the view.

A project that links a native library rawr's runtime also links, such as psm through stacker, now reuses the runtime rawr warmed when both take it from one package at Cargo-compatible versions. Its first run after an install no longer compiles rawr in the project: inboard's 11-minute first start goes away.
A marked function can take a native value of borrows by value, as inboard's `catalog: View<'_>`, for the call alone, and a marked method on it works too.

Inside a marked `view<'a>`, a crate method called on a native `&'a T` lent to the view, such as `inbox.view()`, returns an element that lives as long as the view's own. A crate fn with an `Option<&'a str>` parameter that its output keeps, such as inboard's `sidebar::nav_section(None, ..)`, now imports and runs.

An or-pattern whose alternatives differ only in the crate values they test, such as `Message::Floor(_, floor::Message::Up) | Message::Floor(_, floor::Message::Down)`, no longer fails with a false RAWR-RESOLVE-MATCH. A name missing from one alternative is rustc's E0408, and a binding of another type is E0308. elevato.rs's browser universe now checks.
A marked function takes native values inside an `Option`, a `Vec`, a `Box` or a tuple by value, such as inboard's `home_grid: Option<Element<'a, grid::Message>>`.
A marked function takes a `&[T]` of native values, lent where it is, and passes it on to native functions.

In a marked view, an element from a native function may borrow the view's lent arguments, as inboard's `inbox::view(inbox_state, .., browser_updates, ..)` does. An element that a native part of `self` gives lasts as long as the view's result.

A marked module can name a crate's type alias through a module its `use` binds, such as `extension::registry::Update` after `use model::extension;`. That works in signatures and in `let`s. A crate's or a native module's alias of a std type, such as `type Names = Vec<String>`, now resolves too. Both gave E0425 before.
A crate method whose output borrows its receiver can also take a `&'a T` at that lifetime, as inboard's `wizard.view(catalog, theme)` does from a marked view.

Moving a field out of a crate struct held in a local, as `let task = action.task;`, leaves the struct's other fields for later reads and moves, as rustc does. So `match action.instruction` afterwards works, and so does a destructuring `let Action { instruction, task } = ..` of a crate value.

A build script that declares `cargo::rerun-if-env-changed` for a variable that `[env]` in `.cargo/config.toml` sets now runs as under `cargo run`: rawr gives it the value Cargo gives the script, and a change to `[env]` runs the script again. Before, every crate whose build script uses `cc` failed on a machine whose Cargo config picks a C compiler in `[env]`.
A dependency whose build script isn't named `build.rs`, such as aws-lc-sys's `builder/main.rs`, no longer panics rawr-import with a lost build input.

A native `main`'s calls into marked code run on the thread that makes them, the process's main thread for `main` itself, as cargo's build runs them. A library whose marked `app.rs` starts iced runs from a `main.rs` that only calls it, and a save to `app.rs` shows at iced's next `update` or `view`, keeping the app's state.

A marked function can return a `Result` to native code: a `Result` of crossable types, one whose `Ok` or `Err` is another crate's type, or an alias such as `iced::Result`. The native value itself goes back, so `fn main() -> iced::Result { mycrate::app::run() }` gets iced's own error.

An embedded script can hold inline modules: `Engine::script`, `load`, `compile`, `eval` and `run` resolve `mod m { .. }` with rustc's paths, `pub`, `use`, `super` and E0603, and the host calls the root's functions by name. A file module (`mod m;`) still needs a package.

`call_fn` calls a script function with the parameters it is written with, a `&mut` one included, so `call_fn("update", (model, by))` works. `CallFnOptions::bind_this_ptr` still lends that value apart.
The default call-depth limit is 64 in debug and release builds alike. A script call that finds the host thread's stack nearly full gets more stack, so the limit, not the thread, ends deep recursion.

A package with marked modules builds its native side with the package's own files: `include_bytes!` and `include_str!` through `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` or a path relative to the source file, even outside the package, and its build script, which runs in the package's directory with its build-dependencies. Cargo reruns the script on the files its `rerun-if-changed` lines name, never on a save to a marked module.
A native `src/main.rs` with marked modules no longer prints Cargo's warning that the file is in both the lib and bin targets.

Two projects that share a dependency now both check, whichever runs first. A dependency's shared bindings used to include implementations from other crates the first project had loaded, so the second project failed with `external crate was not loaded`. A crate's bindings now hold only what its own dependencies reach, and bindings saved before this are extracted again once.
A widget that keeps your closure to make its content, as iced's `transition(..)` and `lazy(..)` do, now builds in a view beside widgets that borrow your state. progress_bar's runner now builds.
